The epitope specific mAb KZ52 neutralized a VSV-pseudovirus containing the Zaire Ebola wild type glycoprotein or the variant GP in which the mucin-like and transmembrane domains of EBOV GP were excised and two N-linked glycosylation site motifs (T42V and T230V) were mutated. Neutralization was assayed by the ability to block infection of Vero cells.

The epitope-specific mAb was shown to neutralize transcription and replication competent VLPs. The trVLP is comprised of p4cis-vRNA-RLuc containing EBOV genes (GP1, GP2, VP40, and VP24), non-coding regions and a reporter gene. Neutralization capacity was increased with the GP-specific mAb was used in a cocktail with one or more VP40-specific mAbs.
